title: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation)
description: Lifesaving technique for cardiac arrest victims who are unresponsive and not breathing normally.
prerequisites: Ensure no head/neck injury before moving
warnings: Do not perform CPR on conscious individuals
Use minimum force on infants and children
Switch performers every 2 minutes to maintain quality

steps.stepDescription: Tap the shoulders firmly and shout 'Are you OK?'.
Dial 997 or send the SOS alert. Ask someone to find an AED.
Tilt the head back gently and lift the chin.
Look, listen, and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
Place hands at the center of the chest. Push hard and fast at 100-120 per minute, 2 inches deep.
After 30 compressions, deliver 2 breaths, watching for chest rise.
Repeat 30 compressions and 2 breaths until help arrives or AED is available.

title: Choking (Heimlich Maneuver)
description: Use when someone cannot speak, breathe, or cough due to airway obstruction.
prerequisites: Confirm choking signs (clutching throat, no air)
warnings: Do not perform abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year
Stop if the object is dislodged
Seek medical attention even after success

steps.stepDescription: Ask 'Are you choking?'. If they cannot respond, act fast.
Stand behind the person, wrap your arms around their waist.
Place your fist (thumb side in) just above the navel, well below the breastbone.
Grasp your fist with the other hand and give quick upward thrusts.
Continue until the object is expelled or the person becomes unconscious.
Lay them down and begin CPR. Check the mouth before each breath.

title: Severe Bleeding Control
description: Stop life-threatening external bleeding before help arrives.
prerequisites: Use clean cloth or sterile gauze
warnings: Do not apply tourniquet to neck, head, or torso
Loosen tourniquet only on medical advice

steps.stepDescription: Move the person away from danger if needed.
Use a clean cloth or gauze and press hard on the wound.
If possible, raise the bleeding limb above the heart.
Don't remove soaked dressings. Add new ones on top and keep pressing.
If bleeding cannot be stopped, apply tourniquet 5-7 cm above the wound.
Keep the person warm and lying down until help arrives.

title: Burns Treatment
description: First aid for thermal, chemical, or electrical burns.
prerequisites: Remove non-stuck clothing or jewelry near the burn
warnings: Do not use butter, toothpaste, or oils

steps.stepDescription: Remove the heat source. For chemical burns, brush off dry chemicals first.
Run cool (not cold) water over the burn for 10-20 minutes.
Use sterile non-stick dressing or clean cloth.
If conscious, offer over-the-counter pain medication.
Call 997 for burns larger than the palm, on face/hands/genitals, or with charred skin.

title: Shock Management
description: Recognize and treat shock — pale skin, rapid pulse, confusion, weakness.
prerequisites: Identify cause if possible (bleeding, burn, allergy)
warnings: Do not give food or drink
Do not move person if spinal injury suspected

steps.stepDescription: Position on their back on a flat surface.
Raise legs about 30 cm — unless head, neck, back, or leg injury.
Cover with a blanket. Do not overheat.
Stop bleeding, immobilize fractures.
Be ready to start CPR if breathing stops.
Dial 997 immediately.
